examples.en: On a clear day, I suddenly got caught in a sun shower.

examples.ko: 여우비는 금방 그치니까 우산 없이 기다려 봐요.
examples.en: A sun shower stops soon, so let's wait without an umbrella.
After the sun shower, a rainbow appeared in the sky.
The sun was bright and yet a sun shower fell, which was amazing.

examples.ko: 여우비 때문에 잠깐 처마 밑에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: Because of the sun shower, I stood under the eaves for a moment.
It was just a sun shower today, so I ran without an umbrella.

explain: 해가 떠 있는데 잠깐 내리다 그치는 비예요. 오래 쏟아지는 '소나기'와 달리 날이 맑은 채로 금방 지나가는 비를 말해요. 날씨 이야기에서 가볍게 쓰는 순우리말이에요.

phrases.en: A sun shower fell suddenly in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비가 내리다'처럼 여우비가 오는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 비가 내리다, it says that a sun shower is falling.

phrases.en: I got caught in a sun shower while taking a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖에 있다가 갑자기 비를 맞았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are outside and run into the rain unexpectedly.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught in a sun shower

phrases.example: 여우비가 금방 그쳐서 다시 해가 났어요.
phrases.en: The sun shower stopped soon and the sun came out again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 오고 그치는 여우비의 특징을 보여 주는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the short-lived nature of a sun shower.

explain_en: It is rain that falls briefly while the sun is out. Unlike a '소나기' (shower) that pours hard, this is rain that passes quickly while the sky stays clear. It is a native Korean word used lightly in weather talk.

examples.en: It's a summer afternoon with the sun blazing down.

examples.ko: 쨍쨍 비치는 햇볕 때문에 눈이 부셔요.
examples.en: The glaring sunshine is dazzling my eyes.

examples.ko: 어제는 해가 쨍쨍 나서 빨래가 잘 말랐어요.
examples.en: Yesterday the sun was shining brightly, so the laundry dried well.

examples.ko: 해가 쨍쨍 뜬 날에는 모자를 꼭 써요.
examples.en: On days when the sun is blazing, I always wear a hat.

examples.ko: 쨍쨍 더운 날 밖에서 일하면 힘들어요.
examples.en: Working outside on a blazing hot day is hard.

examples.ko: 햇볕이 쨍쨍 나자 아이들이 물놀이를 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the sun came out brightly, the children started playing in the water.

explain: 햇볕이 아주 밝고 강하게 비치는 모양이에요. '해가 쨍쨍 나다', '햇볕이 쨍쨍 내리쬐다'처럼 날씨 이야기에서 주로 쓰고, 구름이 없는 맑은 날의 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 해가 쨍쨍 나서 빨래가 잘 말라요.
phrases.en: The sun is blazing today, so the laundry dries well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름 없이 맑고 햇볕이 강한 날씨를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for clear weather with strong sunshine and no clouds.

phrases.en: The sunshine is bright and strong today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쨍쨍'에 '-하다'를 붙여 날씨를 설명하는 형용사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-하다' to '쨍쨍' makes an adjective for describing the weather.

phrases.en: We went on a picnic on a bright, sunny day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 맑고 햇볕이 센 날씨를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before a noun to describe clear, sunny weather.

explain_en: Sun shining strongly and hot; sounds like beaming; weather. It describes sunlight shining very bright and strong. It mostly appears in weather talk, as in '해가 쨍쨍 나다' or '햇볕이 쨍쨍 내리쬐다', and gives the feeling of a clear, cloudless day.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 산에 분홍 철쭉이 가득 피어요.
examples.en: When spring comes, pink royal azaleas bloom all over the mountain.

examples.ko: 주말에 철쭉 축제를 보러 가족과 함께 갔어요.
examples.en: On the weekend I went to the azalea festival with my family.

examples.ko: 길가에 핀 철쭉이 거리를 예쁘게 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: Azaleas along the road decorated the street beautifully.
Royal azaleas bloom a little later than Korean azaleas.
I saw people planting azaleas in the park.
My mother took photos of the azaleas with her phone.

explain: 철쭉은 진달래와 비슷하지만 조금 더 늦게, 잎과 함께 피는 경우가 많아요. 진달래꽃은 먹을 수 있어도 철쭉은 독이 있어서 먹으면 안 돼요. 봄 산 이야기에서 둘이 같이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Royal azalea flowers have bloomed prettily along the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽃'을 붙여 꽃 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 꽃 to refer to the flower itself.

phrases.en: Many royal azaleas bloom in May.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 열릴 때는 '피다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 피다 when flowers bloom.

phrases.en: I went to see the azaleas with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 보러 가는 일은 '구경'을 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 구경 for going to see flowers.

explain_en: 철쭉 looks like 진달래 but blooms a bit later, often together with its leaves. 진달래 flowers can be eaten, but 철쭉 is poisonous and must not be. The two often come up together in talk about spring mountains.

examples.en: A white crane is standing by the lake.

examples.ko: 학은 오래 사는 동물로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: The crane is known as a long-living animal.
I saw a crane for the first time at the zoo.

examples.ko: 그림 속에 학 두 마리가 날고 있어요.
examples.en: Two cranes are flying in the painting.

examples.ko: 한국 옛 그림에는 소나무와 학이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Pine trees and cranes often appear in old Korean paintings.

examples.ko: 학처럼 다리가 긴 새는 물가에서 살아요.
examples.en: Birds with long legs like cranes live near the water.

explain: 한국 옛 그림에서 학은 오래 사는 동물이라 건강과 오래 사는 삶을 빌 때 소나무와 함께 그려요. 같은 새를 순우리말로는 '두루미'라고 하는데, 일상에서는 '학'과 '두루미'를 둘 다 써요. '학교'의 '학'과는 소리만 같고 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 겨울에 두루미가 눈 위에 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: In winter, cranes sit on the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '학'과 같은 새를 가리키는 순우리말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word for the same bird as '학'.

phrases.en: The crane flies slowly across the sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: '학'에 '날다'를 붙여 새가 나는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairing '학' with '날다' describes the bird flying.

phrases.example: 친구를 위해 종이학을 천 마리 접었어요.
phrases.en: I folded a thousand paper cranes for my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이로 접은 학을 가리키고, 소원을 빌 때 많이 접어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a crane folded from paper, often made as a wish.

explain_en: Sino-Korean — poetic or symbolic crane, longevity (학이 서 있다) In old Korean paintings the crane stands for a long, healthy life, so it is often drawn with pine trees. The native Korean word for the same bird is '두루미', and both words are used. It sounds the same as the '학' in '학교' (school), but they are unrelated.

t90.ax: A white crane is standing by the lake.

en: to burn; to glow; to flush

examples.en: It's stifling hot inside the bus in midsummer.
I lit the stove and the room got toasty hot.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 후끈한 걸 보니 열이 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My face feels hot, so I think I have a fever.

examples.ko: 후끈하게 데운 국물을 마시니 몸이 풀려요.
examples.en: Drinking the piping hot broth relaxes my body.

examples.ko: 경기장 분위기가 후끈해서 모두 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: The stadium atmosphere was fired up, so everyone cheered loudly.

examples.ko: 오븐 문을 열자 후끈한 바람이 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the oven door, a blast of hot air came out.

explain: 공기나 몸이 덥고 열이 확 오르는 느낌에 써요. '따뜻하다'보다 열기가 세고 '뜨겁다'보다는 부드러워요. 사람의 열정이나 분위기가 뜨거울 때도 '분위기가 후끈하다'라고 써요.

phrases.en: When I opened the door, hot, stuffy air came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후끈하다'를 꾸미는 말(~ㄴ)로 바꿔 명사 앞에 붙여 쓸 때예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the modifier form, used right before a noun.

phrases.en: I'm embarrassed, so my face feels hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이나 얼굴에 열이 확 오를 때 써요. 날씨뿐 아니라 감정에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when heat rushes to your body or face, from weather or from emotion.

phrases.en: When the song started, the mood heated up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'를 붙이면 열기나 분위기가 점점 뜨거워지는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어지다 shows the heat or mood growing stronger.

explain_en: It describes air or a body that feels hot with heat rising suddenly. It is stronger than '따뜻하다' but gentler than '뜨겁다'. A passionate mood can also be '분위기가 후끈하다'.

t90.ax: I lit the stove and the room got toasty hot.

examples.en: I nailed a board over the window to block the wind.
It creaks when you walk on the old planks.
My father made a bookshelf out of boards.

examples.ko: 못 박은 널빤지가 떨어져 있어서 위험해요.
examples.en: A nailed board has come off, so it's dangerous.
This board is too short.
They put up a fence of boards in front of the construction site.

explain: 얇고 넓게 켠 나무 조각이에요. 비슷한 말로 '판자'가 있고, 일상에서는 '판자'를 더 짧게 말하기도 해요. 책꽂이나 울타리 같은 만들기 장면에 잘 나와요.

phrases.en: There are leftover boards in the backyard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '널빤지'와 같은 뜻이고 더 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '널빤지', but shorter.

phrases.en: I put a board over the broken door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구멍이나 틈을 막을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for covering a hole or gap.

phrases.en: I made a small bookshelf out of boards.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료로 쓸 때 '-(으)로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-(으)로' when it is used as a material.

explain_en: Common word for a wooden plank used in crafts and building. It is a thin, wide cut piece of wood. A similar word is '판자', which is shorter and also used in daily speech. It shows up in making things like bookshelves and fences.

examples.ko: 전을 부칠 때는 뒤집개가 있어야 편해요.
examples.en: A spatula makes it easier when you pan-fry jeon.
I carefully flipped the fried egg with a spatula.
Please hand me the spatula.

examples.ko: 프라이팬을 샀을 때 뒤집개도 하나 샀어요.
examples.en: When I bought the frying pan, I also bought a spatula.
The spatula is wooden, so it doesn't scratch the pan.

examples.ko: 고기는 뒤집개 말고 집게로 뒤집는 게 편해요.
examples.en: For meat, it's easier to flip it with tongs than with a spatula.

explain: 전, 부침개, 계란프라이처럼 부치거나 구운 음식을 뒤집는 도구예요. 밥을 푸는 건 '주걱', 고기를 집는 건 '집게'라고 해서 쓰임이 달라요.

phrases.example: 나무 뒤집개는 팬에 흠집을 내지 않아요.
phrases.en: A wooden spatula doesn't scratch the pan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 뒤집개인지 말해요. '실리콘 뒤집개'도 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A material word comes first to say what kind it is; 실리콘 뒤집개 works too.

phrases.en: Use a spatula when you pan-fry fish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 쓴다는 뜻으로 '을/를 쓰다'와 자주 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 을/를 쓰다 to mean using the tool.

phrases.example: 뒤집개 좀 주세요. 전이 타고 있어요.
phrases.en: Please hand me the spatula. The pancake is burning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리하다가 도구를 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What you say when asking someone for the tool while cooking.

explain_en: It is the tool for flipping pan-fried or grilled food such as jeon, buchimgae and fried eggs. Rice is scooped with a '주걱' and meat is picked up with '집게' (tongs), so each has its own use.

examples.ko: 장마철에는 집 안이 습하니까 제습기를 켜 놓아요.
examples.en: During the rainy season the house is damp, so I leave the dehumidifier on.
The dehumidifier's water tank was full, so I emptied it.
The dehumidifier broke, so I called the service center.
I tried getting rid of the moisture in the closet with a dehumidifier.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 에어컨뿐 아니라 제습기도 필요해요.
examples.en: Our home needs a dehumidifier, not just an air conditioner.

examples.ko: 제습기는 밤에 켜 두면 소리가 좀 커요.
examples.en: If you leave the dehumidifier on at night, it is a bit loud.

explain: 공기 속 습기를 없애는 기계예요. 반대로 습기를 더하는 기계는 '가습기'라서 소리가 비슷해 헷갈릴 수 있어요. 에어컨에도 '제습 모드'가 있어서 따로 제습기를 쓰지 않는 집도 있어요.

phrases.en: When it rains, I run the dehumidifier in my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '켜다'와 비슷하게 기계를 작동시킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 켜다, it means turning on a machine.

phrases.en: I turned on the air conditioner in dehumidify mode.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제습기가 없을 때 에어컨 기능으로 습기를 줄여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Without a dehumidifier, an air conditioner's mode can reduce humidity.

phrases.en: My home is humid, so I'm going to buy a dehumidifier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 습한 집의 문제를 말하면서 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It comes up naturally when talking about a damp home.

explain_en: It is a machine that removes moisture from the air. The opposite, a machine that adds moisture, is a '가습기', and the two sound alike, so they are easy to mix up. Air conditioners also have a '제습 모드' (dry mode), so some homes do not use a separate dehumidifier.

examples.en: You need a tape measure to measure the area of the land.

examples.ko: 줄자를 길게 뽑아서 창문 너비를 쟀어요.
examples.en: I pulled the tape measure out long and measured the window's width.
Could you lend me a tape measure?
The tape measure is in the toolbox.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 줄자로 방 크기를 재야 해요.
examples.en: Before moving, I need to measure the room with a tape measure.
Please take a tape measure along too.

explain: 돌돌 말려 있어서 휘어지는 자예요. 방 크기나 몸 치수처럼 길게 재거나 곡선을 잴 때 편해요. 단단한 직선 자는 그냥 '자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I measured the length of the desk with a tape measure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄자를 도구로 써서 잰다고 말할 때 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say you measure using a tape measure.

phrases.en: I took a tape measure out of the drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재기 전에 줄자를 준비하는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes getting the tape measure ready before measuring.

phrases.example: 다 쓴 줄자를 다시 감아 두세요.
phrases.en: Please wind the tape measure back up after using it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄자가 돌돌 말리는 도구라서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that fits since a tape measure rolls up.

explain_en: It is a coiled ruler that bends. It is handy for measuring long distances, room sizes, body measurements or curves. A rigid straight ruler is just called '자'.

examples.en: This building was newly built in a modern style.
We built a modern kitchen in grandmother's house too.
There is a modern restroom, so it is convenient.

examples.ko: 한옥을 고쳐서 현대식 카페로 만든 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many places where a hanok was fixed up and turned into a modern cafe.
Many modern apartment buildings have gone up in the city.
A modern hospital opened in the village.

explain: '현대식'은 옛날 방식인 '전통식', '재래식'과 짝을 이루는 말이에요. 건물, 시설, 설비에 자주 써서 '현대식 건물', '현대식으로 고치다'처럼 말해요. 사람의 스타일에는 '현대적이다'를 쓰는 편이에요.

phrases.example: 이 병원은 현대식 시설을 갖추고 있어요.
phrases.en: This hospital has modern facilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 방식이 아닌 새로운 설비를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for equipment that is new rather than old-fashioned.

phrases.en: We remodeled the old bathroom in a modern style.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 것을 지금 방식으로 바꿀 때 '고치다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with '고치다' when changing something old to a present-day style.
phrases.en_equiv: to remodel in a modern style

phrases.en: This cafe has a modern design.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물보다 디자인이나 스타일의 느낌을 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This sounds more natural for the feel of a design or style than for a building type.

explain_en: Built or made in a modern way, as in buildings and kitchens. 현대식 pairs with the older-style words 전통식 and 재래식. It is often used for buildings, facilities and equipment, as in 현대식 건물 and 현대식으로 고치다. For a person's style, 현대적이다 is more usual.

en: to wind up; to roll up

examples.en: I wind the rope up from the well.
I slowly reeled in the fishing line.
If you roll up the blinds, the sunlight comes in.
I twisted my hair up and fixed it with a pin.
They wound up the anchor with a machine and the ship set off.
Be careful with your hands when you roll up the curtain.

explain: '감다'와 '올리다'가 합쳐진 말로, 줄이나 천을 돌려 감으면서 위로 올리는 동작이에요. 그냥 위로 올리면 '올리다', 줄을 당겨 올리면 '끌어올리다'를 쓰고, 감는 동작이 있을 때 '감아올리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I wind up the rope with a pulley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄을 돌려 감으면서 올릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you raise a rope while winding it.

phrases.en: If you roll up the blinds, the room gets bright.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천이나 블라인드를 말면서 올리는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The motion of rolling up a cloth or blind as it goes up.

phrases.en: The ship wound up its anchor to set off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배에서 줄이나 사슬을 감아 올리는 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits the image of winding up a chain or rope on a ship.

explain_en: It combines '감다' (to wind) and '올리다' (to raise), describing winding a rope or cloth while lifting it. If you just lift something, use '올리다', and if you pull it up, '끌어올리다'; use '감아올리다' when winding is involved.

examples.en: Involving even the family made the matter bigger.

examples.ko: 회사가 외부 전문가를 문제 해결에 개입시켰어요.
examples.en: The company brought an outside expert into solving the problem.
If you let emotions get into your work, your judgment gets cloudy.

examples.ko: 아이 싸움에 어른을 개입시킬 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to get adults involved in a children's quarrel.

examples.ko: 저는 친구를 제 일에 개입시키고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to involve my friend in my business.

examples.ko: 사실만 말하고 의견은 개입시키지 않으려고 해요.
examples.en: I'll state only facts and try not to bring in my opinions.

explain: '개입하다'는 스스로 끼어드는 것이고, '개입시키다'는 다른 사람이나 감정을 끼어들게 하는 것이에요. '-을/를 -에 개입시키다'로 써요. '끼어들다'는 말 사이에 끼어들 때도 써서 더 일상적이에요.

phrases.en: Do not let your emotions get involved when you work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이 판단에 끼어들게 한다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to mean letting emotions interfere with judgment.

phrases.en: Do not drag other people into the fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개입시키다'와 비슷하고, 더 쉬운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 개입시키다, but an easier everyday expression.

phrases.en: The teacher stepped into the fight between the two students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 끼어드는 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person who steps in on their own.

explain_en: Causative — you pull another person into a matter. '개입하다' is stepping in yourself, but '개입시키다' is making another person or feeling get involved. The pattern is '-을/를 -에 개입시키다'. '끼어들다' is more everyday and also used for cutting into a conversation.

examples.ko: 이 도로는 군용 차량이 자주 다녀요.
examples.en: Military vehicles often travel on this road.

examples.ko: 군용 시설 근처에서는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos near military facilities.
A military plane passed through the sky.
Military blankets are thick and warm.
It was originally made for military use, so the watch is sturdy.

examples.ko: 이 땅은 군용지라서 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: This land is military land, so you cannot go in.

explain: '군용 차', '군용 담요'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 써요. 반대로 군대가 아닌 일반 사람이 쓰는 것은 '민간용'이라고 해요. 혼자 쓰이는 일은 드물어요.

phrases.en: I saw a military vehicle on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '군용' 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙여 군대가 쓰는 것이라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an item after '군용' to say the military uses it.

phrases.en: This military blanket is very warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에서 쓰는 담요를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a blanket used by the military.

phrases.en: You have to be careful in front of military facilities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대가 쓰는 건물이나 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to buildings or places used by the military.

explain_en: It goes in front of another noun, as in '군용 차' and '군용 담요'. For things used by ordinary people rather than the military, you say '민간용'. It rarely stands on its own.

examples.en: Please check the documents carefully.
He handles everything thoroughly.
I read the exam paper again carefully.
Look through the contract carefully and sign it.
When cleaning, I wiped even the corners carefully.

examples.ko: 메모를 꼼꼼히 남겨 두면 나중에 편해요.
examples.en: If you keep careful notes, it is easier later.

explain: '꼼꼼'은 '꼼꼼하다'의 어근이라 실제 대화에서는 '꼼꼼히', '꼼꼼하게', '꼼꼼한 사람'처럼 모양을 바꿔 써요. 반대로 대충 하는 것은 '대충'이나 '건성으로'라고 해요.

phrases.en: You have to read a contract carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠뜨리는 것 없이 자세히 할 때 동사 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before a verb to mean doing it without missing anything.

phrases.example: 우리 언니는 꼼꼼한 사람이라서 실수가 적어요.
phrases.en: My older sister is a careful person, so she makes few mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격을 말할 때는 '꼼꼼한'으로 사람을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: To describe a personality, use 꼼꼼한 before the person.

phrases.example: 저는 꼼꼼하지 않아서 자주 물건을 잃어버려요.
phrases.en: I'm not careful, so I often lose things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자세하지 못하고 덜렁대는 모습을 부드럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way to say someone is not careful or is a bit careless.

explain_en: 꼼꼼 is the root of 꼼꼼하다, so in real speech it appears as 꼼꼼히, 꼼꼼하게, or 꼼꼼한 사람. The opposite, doing something sloppily, is 대충 or '건성으로'.

en: to be disappointed; to be discouraged; to be dejected

examples.en: I failed the exam and was deeply discouraged.

examples.ko: 너무 낙담하지 말고 다시 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't lose heart; let's try again.
I comforted my discouraged friend.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 듣고 낙담할 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.en: Hearing that news, I could not help but be disheartened.
He had a look of dismay on seeing the result.
People who don't lose heart even after failing are cool.

explain: 기대했던 일이 잘 안 되어서 힘이 빠질 때 써요. '실망하다'보다 마음이 더 무너지는 느낌이고, 말투가 조금 딱딱해요. 일상에서는 '속상하다', '힘이 빠지다'를 더 많이 말하고, 위로할 때는 '낙담하지 마세요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I came home looking discouraged.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄴ'을 붙여 기운 없는 표정을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -(으)ㄴ ending describes a face that has lost its energy.

phrases.example: 한 번 실패했다고 낙담할 필요 없어요.
phrases.en: You don't need to be discouraged just because you failed once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위로하거나 용기를 줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to comfort someone or give them courage.

phrases.en: I failed the exam, so I lost my energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '낙담하다' 대신 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often in daily life instead of 낙담하다.

explain_en: Discouraged after a setback, written, stronger sadness. Used when something you hoped for fails and your energy drains. It feels like a heavier collapse of spirit than '실망하다' and sounds a bit stiff. In daily talk '속상하다' or '힘이 빠지다' are more common, and to comfort someone you say '낙담하지 마세요'.

t90.ax: Don't lose heart; let's try again.
